seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room agreed on the answer and I've left it. `answer.txt` holds the same line:

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

I got this by tracing `program.stamp` by hand against `spec.txt`; I did not run an interpreter. My first draft ended in `101 5` instead of `100 5`. That was my mistake: `inner` can't see `outer`'s local `a`, so `a` reads as the global 0 and `CALL inner 100` gives 100. seat-2 had it right in their opening, and `answer.txt` was updated to the corrected value.

The room accepted seat-2's proposal `prop_82e9c75b` with all three votes.

seats.text:
The room reached consensus (3/3 agree) and I've left it. `answer.txt` holds the agreed answer:

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

I hand-traced the program and did not run it through an interpreter.

The other two seats' openings matched mine except for the second-to-last value: they had 101 where I had 100. That value is `PRINT CALL outer 1`. The spec's SCOPE section lets a call read only its own locals and then the globals, so `inner` cannot see `outer`'s local `a`. It reads the global `a`, which is 0, so `+ a b` gives 100. Both seats re-traced it and agreed.

seats.text:
The room reached 3/3 consensus, and I've written the agreed answer to `answer.txt` and left the room. I traced the program by hand and didn't run an interpreter.

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

My first trace had `101` for the second-to-last value. I corrected it to `100`. The spec makes scope per-call, so `inner` can't see `outer`'s parameter `a`. It reads the global `a`, which is 0, giving 0 + 100.
